vars.LINE2: More of them are paying closing costs.
vars.SUB: The share of contracts with a seller concession or rate buydown is quietly telling you who has the leverage right now.

vars.TITLE: The decree set a date
vars.LINES:
The house hasn't sold.
The deadline is close.
[[gap]]
Most courts allow an
agreed extension, or a
temporary co-ownership
order while it keeps showing.
[[gap]]
Raise it with the attorney
before it becomes an
[[circle]]emergency.[[/circle]]
vars.NOTE: -> your attorney owns the decree; this is the real estate side of the timeline.

vars.HEADLINE:
You Wrote The Check.
Who's Actually Holding It?
vars.DECK: Usually the title company, not the seller or your agent. Financing, appraisal, and inspection contingencies each protect it differently — know which before you sign.

vars.TITLE: Before assuming full probate
vars.LINES:
A parent has passed away.
The house needs to sell.
[[gap]]
Montana allows a simpler
small estate process below
a certain threshold —
but real property titled
solely in their name
usually needs its own
[[circle]]path.[[/circle]]
vars.NOTE: -> confirm which path applies with the attorney handling the estate.

vars.HEADLINE:
Evergreen
[[i]]the middle ground[[/i]]
vars.SUB: Closer to town than Kila, quieter than either city center — a shorter commute to Kalispell and Whitefish than most buyers think to check.

vars.LINE2: "I don't know" still has to be said.
vars.SUB: Montana's disclosure form runs on what you actually know, not speculation — and sitting on a known issue is a different problem entirely.

vars.TAG: West and Company · How We Work
vars.HEADLINE:
Feel It Later.
Decide Clean Now.
vars.DECK: A lowball offer or a heated inspection fight still lands. The discipline is keeping the next decision clean while the feeling gets handled on its own time.
